investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-25T12:26–12:27Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurred before any agent was provisioned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning path — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" for every POST /api/agents call. Because all three sibling checks share the same upstream provisioning call and all returned the identical error message within a ~34-second window, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway or the network path between production-api and that ELB, not to individual check logic or eval runner code.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. POST /api/agents returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway for every remote-agents check. Because the eval runner calls createAgent as the prerequisite step before any runtime or state checks, the gateway failure cascaded to all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime), each returning the identical error message and producing zero evidence. investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=715, max=300)
investigations.summary: The eval-only check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 715 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, confirming this is an isolated snapshot-staleness failure, not a broader site or infrastructure outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot's `source` field confirms it is produced by `github-actions` (evidence: failed-check.evidence), and the measured age of 715 minutes is more than double the allowed maximum, indicating the workflow was either skipped, failed silently, or was not triggered for an extended period (~11.9 hours). This is an eval infrastructure / workflow scheduling failure, not a user-facing site outage — the /observability page itself returned HTTP 200 (evidence: sibling.public-observability-page).

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot was not triggered or did not complete successfully for approximately 11.9 hours prior to the eval run at 2026-08-25T12:27:14Z. The snapshot's source='github-actions' field (failed-check.evidence) confirms this workflow is the sole publisher.

Possible: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) and did not update the published status.json, leaving the stale file in place.
Possible: A GitHub Actions schedule trigger was skipped due to repository inactivity, a GitHub platform incident, or a workflow concurrency/queue issue that caused the scheduled run to be dropped.

Less likely: The workflow ran and published a new snapshot, but a GitHub Pages CDN caching layer served the stale file to the eval runner. This would be inconsistent with the 715-minute age gap but cannot be fully ruled out without inspecting workflow run logs.

Less likely: A configuration drift between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's maxAgeMinutes=300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482/486) means the eval contract is stricter than the registry config, but the 715-minute age violates both thresholds, so this discrepancy is not the proximate cause of this specific failure.
